body.heading: Where in the world is Canada?
paragraphs: Canada is a country in Northern America, which is part of North America.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Canada is Ottawa. Ottawa is the capital, chosen by Queen Victoria in 1857. Toronto is the biggest city, but Ottawa is where parliament meets on Parliament Hill.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Canada speak English and French. English and French are both official languages of Canada — road signs and cereal boxes use both.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Canada is the Canadian dollar.

body.heading: How big is Canada?
paragraphs: Canada covers about 9,985,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. It is the largest country in North America.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: Canada has more natural lakes than any other country. Nobody knows exactly how many lakes Canada has — the count runs into the hundreds of thousands.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: In the Rockies, Lake Louise glows turquoise beneath glaciers. Families canoe its waters, ride the Banff gondola and watch for elk and bears.
Niagara's Horseshoe Falls pour 2,800 tonnes of water a second over the cliff. Boat rides sail into the mist and tunnels run behind the falls.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Canada on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: Canada in one breath: a country in Northern America, capital Ottawa, where people speak English and pay with the Canadian dollar.
materials: A globe, atlas or world map (to find Canada)
Paper and crayons or pencils for the screen-free mission
supervision: Read this one together: a grown-up can help with tricky place names and hunt for Canada on the map as you read.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity is involved.
If your family ever visits the watery places in this article, water fun in Canada always needs a grown-up watching closely.
